item.title: Why AI Agents May Require a New Security Operations Model
item.description:
Organizations are rapidly adopting AI agents to retrieve data, invoke tools, automate workflows, interact with applications, and increasingly make decisions on behalf of users. As these agents become part of the enterprise workforce, they introduce an entirely new security surface. A compromised endpoint can spread malware. A compromised identity can access sensitive data. A compromised AI agent can do both — while also reasoning, invoking tools, interacting with other agents, and executing actions at machine speed.

item.title: Building a CCF Nested API Pull Connector: A Technical Lab Walkthrough
item.description: This post walks through building a Microsoft Sentinel Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) RestApiPoller connector that uses the nested API polling pattern. The nested pattern exists for a specific reason: many enterprise APIs do not return enriched records from a single call. Instead, they use a two-step model: a list endpoint that returns identifiers, followed by a detail endpoint that accepts one identifier and returns the full record. item.title: End VPN gaps with identity-first access
item.description: Traditional VPNs extend network access—but they were not built continuously evaluate identity, device posture, location, user risk, or session context. Zero Trust closes this gap by putting identity and policy at the center of every access decision. Microsoft principles are simple: verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, and assume breach.
